utterance: Hi Chloe, come on in and take a seat. I see from the booking note that you've been having some burning when passing urine since yesterday. Could you tell me a bit more about what's been happening?
reply: It started yesterday morning, so about a day and a half ago. It stings and burns, and it is worst right at the end of going to the toilet. I am going constantly, about every half hour, and only a little bit comes out and I have to rush. It is also a bit cloudy and smells, but I haven't seen any blood.

reply: Just a bit of an ache low down in my tummy, but nothing in my back. I have not had any fevers or shivers, and I am eating normally and haven't been sick.

utterance: Chloe, your urine dipstick shows signs of a bladder infection, and the pregnancy test is negative. Your vital signs and examination are all reassuring, with no signs of the infection affecting your kidneys. Just before we sort out treatment, have you ever had a sexually transmitted infection check since being with your current partner, or is there anything else on your mind today?
reply: No, I haven't had one since being with him, and there is nothing else on my mind.

awards.label: First-line antibiotic: nitrofurantoin 100 mg 6-hourly for 5 days, fosfomycin 3 g once, or trimethoprim 300 mg daily for 3 days

utterance:
So what you have is an acute uncomplicated bladder infection, also called cystitis. I've prescribed a 3-day course of an antibiotic called trimethoprim 300 mg—you just take one tablet once a day, ideally at night before bed, for 3 days. This antibiotic will not interfere with your contraceptive pill unless you were to have severe vomiting or diarrhoea.

To help with the stinging and burning in the meantime, make sure you drink plenty of water to stay well hydrated, and you can use over-the-counter urinary alkaliniser sachets (like Ural) or simple pain relief like paracetamol or ibuprofen if needed. Notice though that if you take urinary alkalinisers, try to space them out by a couple of hours from your antibiotic, and to help prevent future infections, passing urine soon after sex can also be really helpful.

Your symptoms should start improving within 48 hours. However, if your symptoms aren't getting better after 2 to 3 days, or if they come back after finishing the tablets, please come back and see me so we can send a urine sample off to the lab. Most importantly, if you develop a fever, chills, pain in your back or side, nausea or vomiting, or start feeling much more unwell, seek urgent medical care right away as that could mean the infection is spreading to your kidneys. Do you have any questions about this plan?
reply: Can I just grab the script now so I can get back to work?

utterance: Of course, the prescription is all ready for you. Hope you feel much better very soon, and take care!
